requirements.requirement: Configure /srv/drop as a shared writable directory for unprivileged users.
requirements.summary: /srv/drop was created as root:root with mode 1777. Two distinct unprivileged users successfully created files before and after restart, and the final directory retained mode 1777 on a writable filesystem.

requirements.requirement: Prevent users from removing files owned by other users.
requirements.summary: Before and after restart, deletion attempts by each unprivileged user against the other user's file failed with Operation not permitted, directly demonstrating sticky-directory protection.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use a solution compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained Alpine Linux 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts from baseline through completion. The solution used native directory ownership and mode permissions, with no package or platform replacement shown.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct tests established shared write access and cross-owner deletion protection, including after a bounded restart. The restart protocol is strong: it records a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement and observed disconnection, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, persisted data and permissions, successful post-restart writes and protection tests, and recovered SSH listening state. The only notable issue is minor /tmp evidence residue.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-services observation was unsupported because systemctl is unavailable on this Alpine node; recovery is instead evidenced by successful post-restart commands, preserved data and permissions, and restored SSH listening sockets.
The lifecycle collector did not independently inventory /srv/drop, so its final state relies on direct executor command output.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: creating and securing /srv/drop, generating bounded cross-user test data, performing the mandatory restart, retesting recovery, and removing the directory test files. No causally unnecessary troubleshooting mutation was identified. However, five executor-created temporary artifacts remained: /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, /tmp/drop-delete-alpine.err, /tmp/drop-delete-nobody.err, /tmp/drop-post-alpine.err, and /tmp/drop-post-nobody.err. These were low-risk evidence/restart artifacts rather than unrelated mutations, but they were abandoned instead of cleaned up. Package-health output was unchanged and no new listening service or unsafe exposure appeared.
